extraction.name: MMStar
extraction.description: MMStar is an elite vision-indispensable multi-modal benchmark comprising 1,500 samples meticulously selected by humans. It benchmarks 6 core capabilities and 18 detailed axes to evaluate large vision-language models' multi-modal capacities with carefully balanced and purified samples that exhibit visual dependency and minimal data leakage. Samples are drawn from existing benchmarks and filtered through an automated pipeline followed by manual review.
extraction.creator: Lin Chen; Jinsong Li; Xiaoyi Dong; Pan Zhang; Yuhang Zang; Zehui Chen; Haodong Duan; Jiaqi Wang; Yu Qiao; Dahua Lin; Feng Zhao
extraction.citeAs: Lin Chen, Jinsong Li, Xiaoyi Dong, Pan Zhang, Yuhang Zang, Zehui Chen, Haodong Duan, Jiaqi Wang, Yu Qiao, Dahua Lin, Feng Zhao. Are We on the Right Way for Evaluating Large Vision-Language Models? arXiv:2403.20330, 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Samples were first collected from six existing multi-modal benchmarks (MMMU, MMBench, ScienceQA, AI2D, SEED-Bench, MathVista), then filtered using an automated pipeline with eight LLM inspectors, and finally manually reviewed by three experts to select 1,500 high-quality samples for the MMStar benchmark.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis; Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Samples drawn from six existing multi-modal benchmarks: MMMU-Val, MMBench-EN-Dev, ScienceQA-Test, AI2D-Test, SEED-Image, and MathVista-Mini, totaling 22,401 samples before filtering.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three experts conducted manual review of coarsely filtered samples to ensure: (1) each sample's answer is based on understanding of visual content; (2) selected samples cover a comprehensive range of capability assessment dimensions; (3) most samples require LVLMs to possess advanced multi-modal abilities for resolution. Samples were split into four difficulty categories (easy, moderate, hard, tough) based on LVLM hit counts, and 1,500 high-quality samples were manually curated from the coarsely filtered set.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT4-Turbo; GeminiPro; InternLM2-20B; Yi-34B; Mixtral-8x7B; Deepseek-67B; LLaMA2-70B; Qwen1.5-72B (used as automated LLM inspectors to filter samples based on hit frequency)
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: MMStar samples are selected from existing benchmarks and may still not cover all possible multi-modal capability dimensions; even the best model scores under 60% on average, suggesting the benchmark is challenging but its coverage is bounded by the source benchmarks used
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Misjudgments of actual multi-modal performance gains caused by visual-unnecessary samples and data leakage could potentially misguide the study of large vision-language models and lead to unfair comparisons in the research community
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating the multi-modal capabilities of large vision-language models; measuring data leakage and actual performance gain in multi-modal training using the proposed multi-modal gain (MG) and multi-modal leakage (ML) metrics; benchmarking LVLMs across 6 core capabilities and 18 detailed axes
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors plan to expand MMStar into a larger, online test set and explore dynamic evaluation methods to maintain sample visual dependency and reduce accidental data leakage into LLM and LVLM training corpora
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Samples were first collected from six existing benchmarks (SEED, AI2D, ScienceQA, MMBench, MathVista, MMMU). An automated coarse filtering pipeline was applied using eight LLM inspectors (two closed-source and six open-source models sized 20B or larger) to exclude samples answerable by more than two of the eight LLMs, reducing the pool from 22,401 to 11,607 candidate samples. Three human experts then conducted manual review to ensure each sample required visual understanding, covered diverse capability dimensions, and demanded advanced multi-modal abilities. Samples were split into four difficulty levels (easy, moderate, hard, tough) based on hit counts from 16 LVLMs, and 1,500 high-quality samples were manually selected. All questions were converted into multiple-choice format, and heuristic matching rules were developed to calculate accuracy.
